emit-range == (lambda (from to next)
  (if (<= from to)
      (IO-THEN (UART-TX from)
               (emit-range (1+ from) to next))
      next))

  (emit-range 48 57
    (emit-range 65 90
      (emit-range 97 122
        (UART-TX 10))))
  (IO-RETURN NIL))

image.source:
; Caesar cipher over the simulated UART. Letters rotate by +4; other bytes pass
; through unchanged. ESC (byte 27) stops the loop. Ctrl-C stops the host process.
;
; Run with:
;   uv run thor examples/uart-caesar-plus4.thor

rot-upper == (lambda (byte)
  (+ 65 (MOD (+ (- byte 65) 4) 26)))

rot-lower == (lambda (byte)
  (+ 97 (MOD (+ (- byte 97) 4) 26)))

rot == (lambda (byte)
  (if (AND (>= byte 65) (<= byte 90))
      (rot-upper byte)
      (if (AND (>= byte 97) (<= byte 122))
          (rot-lower byte)
          byte)))

loop == (lambda (ignored)
  (IO-BIND (UART-RX)
    (LAMBDA (byte)
      (if (= byte NIL)
          (loop NIL)
          (if (= byte 27)
              (IO-RETURN NIL)
              (IO-THEN (UART-TX (rot byte))
                       (loop NIL)))))))

(loop NIL)

scope_limits: The RTL UART example checks are output prefixes at quantum 5; full outputs and halts were checked in the typed hardware source and on the board.
Alphanumerics uses quantum 20; budget 5 fills the graph with deferred arguments after printing the digits.
No physical power-removal test was performed by this script; a reset from configuration flash was verified.
validation_notes: The exact-command observer drains UART input after blocking JTAG status samples before deciding whether a halt completed the output. An initial observer race was corrected and all three commands passed on rerun.
29 focused pytest tests passed after switching defaults; changed small Python files pass Ruff and git diff --check passed.
